findings.message: 6 headline(s) switch typeface or to italic mid-line (the "one italic serif word" move).
findings.fix: Set the whole headline in one face. Emphasis comes from the words.
A page needs about five: display, heading, lead, body, small.

findings.message: No video anywhere on the page.
findings.fix: Look for one honest clip with scripts/assets.mjs --video (the place, the material, the process) and use it as a muted loop with a poster frame. Defend its absence only if no clip fits the subject.

findings.message: A section keeps its content on one side and leaves 963px of the width empty: div.work-head.shell.
findings.fix: Fill the other side with what the section has (its picture, a second column, the figure), or defend the void in one sentence.

findings.message: 1 stretch(es) of the page hold nothing at all: 884px at 10696px (the screen is 900px tall).
findings.fix: Close the gap: a section gap is 120–240px on desktop and 72–112px on a phone. Look for a min-height: 100vh on a short section, an empty grid row, a hidden element still holding its space, or a reveal that never fired. A deliberate rest is a placed picture or colour field, not nothing.

findings.message: 60% of the first screen is one empty block (1440×540px at 0,120).
findings.fix: Place the void on purpose or fill it: move the picture, the film or one fact into it, grow the headline to meet it, or shrink the screen to its content. A void reads as placed only when something closes it on the far side and it is the screen's one rest.

findings.message: Left-aligned text starts at 10 different lines (72px, 40px, 963px, 29px, 1124px, 2132px, 3140px); the three most used hold only 57% of it.
findings.fix: Pick two or three anchor lines from the grid and start every heading and paragraph on one of them.

findings.message: Large text lies under another element at some scroll position: "2026 · NLL Academy · Full-Stack Developer" (screen 7, 100% hidden)
findings.fix: Nothing may sit on top of a headline or statement. Move the picture, shorten the pinned run, or raise the text above it (z-index) and give it a ground.

findings.message: Pinned large text slides across pictures while the page scrolls: "ABOUT" (screen 2, 100% over a picture); "Documents in. Answers out." (screen 3, 37% over a picture); "FULL-STACK DEVELOPER" (screen 5, 61% over a picture)
findings.fix: Jurors read a pinned title crossing drawings or photographs as a collision. Keep the pictures in the column the title does not occupy, or unpin it.

findings.message: The same large text stays on screen for 4 screens in a row: "WHERE I’VE BEEN"; "FULL-STACK DEVELOPER"
findings.fix: A pinned element earns two screens, and something must change at each. Shorten the run or give every screen its own content.

findings.message: 1 headline(s) wrap past two lines at 768px: "Lira Lira SOP Automation SOP Automation Lira Lir" → 3 lines (13 words, 26.7px)
findings.fix:
Cut words first (a headline is a title, not a sentence). Then give it a wider measure. Lower the size only as a last resort and never below the scale you chose. A real statement paragraph belongs in a

or

at 32px or less.

findings.message: The h1 is a bare name ("PRINCE JOSHI") and nothing else on the first screen says what this is.
findings.fix: Keep the name if it leads, and give the line under it (18px or more) the plain words: what it is, for whom, where or when. In the study of 97 Sites of the Day, first screens that named nothing lost usability and content points.
